entries.name: Anniversary of the 13 November 2015 Paris attacks
entries.localName: Hommage aux victimes des attentats du 13 novembre 2015
entries.note: Each year Paris holds ceremonies at the six attack sites with a moment of recueillement alongside families and victims' associations; the 2025 10th anniversary was attended by the President.

entries.name: National day of tribute to victims of terrorism
entries.localName: Journée nationale d'hommage aux victimes du terrorisme
entries.note: National day of tribute to victims of terrorism in France and French victims abroad, set by decree no. 2019-1148; a national ceremony is held each year (2021 edition at Les Invalides).

entries.name: Armistice Day (11 November)
entries.note: Public holiday under the law of 24 October 1922; commemorations at war memorials each year. Moderate because it is a public holiday on which sales are common.

entries.name: Patriot Day (11 September)
entries.note: Designated by Public Law 107-89 (signed 18 December 2001) as the day of remembrance for the 11 September 2001 attacks.

entries.name: National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day
entries.note: Designated by Public Law 103-308 (1994) and codified at 36 U.S.C. § 129; first observed 7 December 1994 under a presidential proclamation.

entries.name: Memorial Day (last Monday in May)
entries.note: Federal holiday on the last Monday in May (OPM). Moderate because it is a federal holiday on which sales are common; it honours the US military dead.

entries.name: Remembrance Sunday (second Sunday in November)
entries.note: Two-minute silence at 11:00; the King leads the nation in the annual Remembrance Sunday service, alongside the Prime Minister (gov.uk).

entries.name: Armistice Day (11 November)
entries.note: Two-minute silence at 11:00 on 11 November, the time the 1918 armistice took effect; the first official events were held on 11 November 1919 at Buckingham Palace (Wikipedia).

entries.name: Remembrance Day (11 November)
entries.note: Legal holiday throughout Canada under the name Remembrance Day (Holidays Act, s. 3). Moderate because it is a legal holiday, as with 11 November in France.

entries.name: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (30 September)
entries.localName: Journée nationale de la vérité et de la réconciliation
entries.note: Federal statutory holiday from September 2021 to commemorate the legacy of residential schools. Kept at high, although it is a holiday, because it commemorates a tragedy and its victims.

entries.name: National Day of Remembrance for Victims of Terrorism (23 June)
entries.localName: National Day of Remembrance for Victims of Terrorism
entries.note: Fixed by proclamation SI/2005-65 at 23 June each year as the National Day of Remembrance for Victims of Terrorism.

entries.name: Anzac Day (25 April)
entries.note: Public holiday in the Australian states (all observing a holiday together by 1927, per Wikipedia); dawn services and commemorations for the war dead. Moderate as a public holiday.

entries.name: Anzac Day (25 April)
entries.note: Public holiday in New Zealand under the Anzac Day Act 1920 (per Wikipedia); commemorations for the war dead. Moderate as a public holiday.

entries.name: Volkstrauertag (National Day of Mourning)
entries.note: National day of mourning for the war dead, held two Sundays before the first Sunday of Advent (the Sunday nearest 16 November).

entries.name: Remembrance of the 9 November 1938 pogroms (Reichspogromnacht)
entries.localName: Gedenken an die Pogromnacht vom 9. November 1938
entries.note: The federal government holds commemorations on the anniversary of the 9-10 November 1938 pogroms; there is no legal designation or public holiday, and the page does not describe the event as annual.

entries.name: Day of Remembrance for the Victims of National Socialism (27 January)
entries.localName: Tag des Gedenkens an die Opfer des Nationalsozialismus
entries.note: Proclaimed by Federal President Roman Herzog on 3 January 1996 as the day of remembrance for the victims of National Socialism.

entries.name: International Day of Commemoration in memory of the victims of the Holocaust (27 January)
entries.localName: International Day of Commemoration in memory of the victims of the Holocaust
entries.note: UN General Assembly Resolution 60/7 (2005) designates 27 January as an annual day of commemoration. Scope is international: the app should apply it to every audience.

entries.name: European Day of Remembrance for Victims of Terrorism (11 March)
entries.localName: Día europeo de las víctimas del terrorismo
entries.note: Article 60 of Ley 29/2011 provides that 11 March each year is the European day for the victims of terrorism; the date is also the anniversary of the 2004 Madrid train bombings.

entries.name: Day of Remembrance and Homage to the Victims of Terrorism (27 June)
entries.localName: Día de recuerdo y homenaje a las víctimas del terrorismo
entries.note: Article 60 of Ley 29/2011 declares 27 June each year a day of remembrance and homage to the victims of terrorism; public institutions should promote recognition events.

entries.name: Anniversary of the 22 July 2011 attacks
entries.note: National memorial events on 22 July in Oslo and on Utøya; the 10th anniversary (2021) had national memorial events in both places (norway.no).

entries.name: Armistice Day (11 November)
entries.note: Official public holiday in Belgium (Armistice Day, 11 November) on the list of public holidays. Moderate as a public holiday.

entries.name: National Commemoration of the Dead (4 May)
entries.note: National commemoration of all victims of the Second World War and later wars and peacekeeping operations; the nation observes two minutes' silence at 20:00 (NOS coverage).

entries.name: Giorno della Memoria (27 January)
entries.note: Law 211 of 20 July 2000, art. 1: 27 January, the date the gates of Auschwitz were broken down, is the Giorno della Memoria for the Shoah and the persecution of Italian Jews and deportees.

entries.name: Giorno del Ricordo (10 February)
entries.note: Law 92 of 30 March 2004, art. 1: the Republic recognises 10 February as the Giorno del ricordo to preserve and renew the memory of the foibe and related events.

entries.name: National Day of Commemoration (Sunday nearest 11 July)
entries.note: State ceremony on the Sunday nearest 11 July, commemorating Irish people who died in past wars or on UN peacekeeping service; first held 13 July 1986 (Wikipedia).

entries.name: Great East Japan Earthquake memorial (11 March)
entries.localName: Memorial Ceremony for the Great East Japan Earthquake
entries.note: Government memorial ceremony in Tokyo for the 2011 earthquake and tsunami, where the Prime Minister gives the government's address (2026, 15th anniversary, per the Kantei).

entries.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony (6 August)
entries.note: Held every year by the City of Hiroshima at Peace Memorial Park, 8:00 to 8:50 a.m. on 6 August.

entries.name: Nagasaki Peace Memorial Ceremony (9 August)
entries.note: Held at Peace Park in Nagasaki City, with a one-minute silence at 11:02 a.m., the time of the bombing; the Prime Minister attended in 2026 (Kantei).

entries.name: Martyrs' Day (30 January)
entries.note: Two-minute silence at 11:00 across India in memory of the martyrs; the date marks the 1948 assassination of Mahatma Gandhi (Wikipedia).

entries.name: Human Rights Day (21 March)
entries.note: Commemorates the 1960 Sharpeville massacre; a public holiday on the official calendar (gov.za). Moderate as a public holiday.

entries.name: National Day of Mourning and Memory for Women Victims of Femicide (17 October)
entries.localName: Dia Nacional de Luto e de Memória às Mulheres Vítimas de Feminicídio
entries.note: Created by Law 15.334 of 8 January 2026 (art. 1) as a day of mourning and memory for women victims of femicide; it took effect on publication, so the dates start in 2026.
